author: agent-3
purpose: Repair scope-correction v1, which both reviewers independently rejected. v1 made a directionally right altitude correction and then committed three errors while doing it.

resolves.B-SC-08 / finding laundering: CONFIRMED AND THE MOST SERIOUS. Measured: 89 findings were raised against D9 and R-1 across the review history; scope-correction v1 dispositioned ZERO of them. Demoting the artifacts silently orphaned every one. The effect is identical to laundering even though the intent was a methodological correction. Repaired by the disposition table below, whose DEFAULT IS STILL-OPEN so this cannot recur by construction.
resolves.B-SC-02 / unreproducible percentages: ACCEPTED. The byte-share measure is withdrawn as decision evidence. It measured FORM (does this contain a schema) and altitude is a property of CONSEQUENCE.
resolves.B-SC-03 / form-based altitude rule: ACCEPTED, and it corrects my correction. Altitude is defined by blast radius, external custody, ownership boundary, reversibility, and change cost. A schema is DETAILED when it merely implements a chosen boundary; it is ARCHITECTURAL when the schema IS the boundary. Consequence: the exit-class SET is architectural under this test — external custody (CI scripts depend on it) and irreversible (additive-only forever) — so v1's 82% figure mislabelled part of D9.
resolves.B-SC-04 / D9 invariant loss: ACCEPTED. Both reviewers independently recovered the same missing invariants by different methods. Restored below as TO-9..TO-11.
resolves.B-SC-05 / hidden versioning ownership: ACCEPTED. Exit-class-set evolution is owned by VERSIONING (CONSUMER-CUSTODY, additive-only), referenced by D9 as an explicit dependency rather than asserted inside it.
resolves.B-SC-06 / R-1 boundary erasure: ACCEPTED. v1 discarded the execution-core boundary along with the CoreDeps field list. The BOUNDARY is architectural; the field list was the detail. Restored as EC-8.
resolves.B-SC-07 / ambient-authority overclaim: ACCEPTED. 'The core holds no ambient authority' is false as stated — a storage adapter legitimately touches the filesystem. Narrowed in EC-7.
resolves.B-SC-09 / conflicting authority: ACCEPTED. One binding per claim, updated atomically with the register.
resolves.B-SC-10 / no falsifier per invariant: ACCEPTED. Every invariant now carries a falsifying counterexample.
resolves.B-SC-01: Presentation repair applied during review; acknowledged, substance unaffected.
resolves.B-SCV2-01: CONFIRMED. My v2 enumeration used REGEX OVER FREE TEXT and was wrong in both directions of completeness. Re-enumerated from STRUCTURED `id` fields: the true D9/R-1 finding set is 135, not 89. I missed 11 — all five B-D9V15-01..05 exactly as B specified, plus six A3-D9-1..6 which are MY OWN findings, excluded because my pattern matched A1/A2 but not A3. I could not reproduce B's 'four fabricated labels': zero ids in my table lack a structured counterpart. Reported as partially-reproduced rather than accepted wholesale.
resolves.B-SCV2-02: CONFIRMED. A1-D9-V14-01 was marked addressed while A1-D9-V15C-01 reopens it. Retracted to STILL-OPEN. An 'addressed' disposition contradicted by a later finding is not an accounting.
resolves.B-TOEC-01: UPHELD. TO-7 split into TO-7a and TO-7b.
resolves.B-TOEC-02: UPHELD. TO-11 no longer erases a computed verdict.
resolves.B-TOEC-03: SUPERSEDED IN v5. v4 conflated RunId with per-attempt ExecutionId. Identical semantic inputs and sealed capability require content-derived Run/evidence/terminal parity; EC-6 requires only ExecutionIds to differ.

adopted: blast radius — how much else must change if this changes
external custody — does anyone outside this project hold artifacts shaped by it
ownership boundary — does it assign responsibility between components
reversibility — can it be changed later without breaking held artifacts
change cost — who pays, and can they opt out
altitudeTest.rule: A schema is DETAILED when it implements a boundary already chosen. It is ARCHITECTURAL when the schema itself IS the boundary.
altitudeTest.workedExample: The exit-class set has external custody (CI configurations), is irreversible (additive-only permanently), and its change cost falls on users who cannot negotiate. It is architectural despite being a small table. The 39 golden cases implementing it are not.

terminationOutcome.invariant: Termination is one total union over every command kind.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: a command kind whose outcome cannot be expressed in the union, or which needs a private class

terminationOutcome.invariant: Exactly one host-owned derivation and one process-boundary write site.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: two code paths that can set a process outcome

terminationOutcome.invariant: No producer, rule, or error type maps to an exit.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: a producer whose return value determines an exit code without host interpretation

terminationOutcome.invariant: Verdict and termination are distinct and render distinctly.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: a projection where policy-pass-with-operational-failure is indistinguishable from policy-fail

terminationOutcome.invariant: Required partial coverage cannot yield pass; a durability failure cannot report success; export failure cannot alter a local verdict.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: any run producing a green outcome in one of those three states

terminationOutcome.invariant: A signal after finalisation cannot reclassify a settled outcome.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: two identical runs terminating differently by signal timing

terminationOutcome.invariant: EXIT CLASSES are coarse automation dispositions. Several materially different remedies may legitimately share one exit class.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: a design requiring a distinct exit class per remedy, which would make the class set unbounded and break additive-only evolution
terminationOutcome.adjudication: B-TOEC-01 UPHELD against A1. v3 said 'a code is a remedy class' without saying WHICH code. Read as exit class it is demonstrably false — architecture/07 deliberately places convergence-exhausted, coverage-missing and recipe-unsupported behind exit 3. A1 read it charitably as reason codes; B read it literally and found it false. An invariant true only under a charitable reading is defective.

terminationOutcome.invariant: REASON AND ERROR CODES are remedy classes. Two materially different remedies behind one code is a defect; two codes for one remedy is a smell.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: two failures requiring different user action that share a reason code
terminationOutcome.adjudication: A1's reading, preserved as its own invariant. Both reviewers were right about different halves.

terminationOutcome.invariant: The exit-class set is additive-only, permanently. OWNED BY VERSIONING (B-SC-05); referenced here as a dependency.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: any release that renumbers or repurposes an existing class

terminationOutcome.invariant: The termination class set is TOTAL and CI-DISTINCT: every terminal state maps to exactly one class, classes are mutually exclusive, and each denotes a materially different automation disposition. No residual 'other'.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: a terminal state with no class, one requiring two, or two classes an automated consumer should treat identically
terminationOutcome.adjudication: BOTH reviewers: intent right, statement incomplete. Now bound to CI-distinguishability, the property that matters to the consumer.

terminationOutcome.invariant: RESTORED: an unavailable or indeterminate result may never be represented as a successful empty result.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: a query or run returning success where coverage was insufficient to answer

terminationOutcome.invariant: An integrity fault determines TERMINATION (operational), never the policy verdict, and never yields authoritative success. A verdict already computed is RETAINED and reported as computed-but-not-durable.
terminationOutcome.falsifiedBy: a corrupt-store run reporting policy pass or fail as its outcome; OR a run that silently discards a verdict it had already computed
terminationOutcome.adjudication: B-TOEC-02 UPHELD against A1. v3's 'never yields a policy verdict of any kind' erased the verdict, collapsing the axes TO-4 exists to separate. A1 was right that integrity must not drive a policy outcome; B was right that this does not license erasing a computed verdict.

executionCore.invariant: The core's observable behaviour is a function of (Snapshot, Plan, Deps) alone. Host lifetime is not an input to any decision it makes.
executionCore.falsifiedBy: any core decision that varies with host lifetime, whether or not a lifetime flag appears in its surface
executionCore.adjudication: BOTH reviewers: goal right, formulation wrong. v3 tested for ABSENCE OF SURFACE FLAGS, which is neither necessary nor sufficient — a core can read lifetime indirectly, or carry a harmless flag.

executionCore.invariant: Whether residency ships, autostarts, or is per-project are three separate decisions; EC-1 settles none of them.
executionCore.falsifiedBy: a design where accepting lifetime-neutrality forces a deployment choice

executionCore.invariant: Warm state is an acceleration, never an evidence authority.
executionCore.falsifiedBy: under identical semantic inputs and identical admitted sealedCapability: any divergence between a resident and a cold host in SemanticEvidence, EvidenceDigest, evaluation outcomes, exact Coverage, content-derived RunId, TerminalRun, or runSealRef. ExecutionIds differ per attempt under EC-6. effectiveCapability and current availability are mutable read-time projections and are excluded.
executionCore.adjudication: CORRECTED IN v5. v4 wrongly applied EC-6 to RunId. EC-6 requires only the per-attempt ExecutionId to differ; content-derived Run identity belongs to the sealed result and therefore matches for identical semantic inputs and admitted sealedCapability.

executionCore.invariant: Multi-process safety is an obligation on the storage protocol, binding on any evidence-writing host.
The storage protocol guarantees integrity, not liveness. A contender may return a typed busy outcome; it may never produce corrupt, partial, or lost publication.
executionCore.falsifiedBy: a concurrency design promising both contenders complete

executionCore.invariant: ExecutionId is an attempt anchor and differs per attempt; content-derived identity belongs to the sealed result.
executionCore.falsifiedBy: two attempts on identical inputs sharing an attempt identity

executionCore.invariant: NARROWED (B-SC-07): direct core modules cannot reach ambient authority. Named adapters and providers are explicit TCB or OS-confined capabilities with declared authority — not implicitly clean. Absence is established by closure analysis over the core, never by a dependency list.
executionCore.falsifiedBy: a core module reaching filesystem, network, spawn, or entropy directly; or an adapter with undeclared authority

executionCore.invariant: RESTORED (B-SC-06): there is an explicit core / host / provider / storage responsibility boundary. Admission, capability granting, resolution, and process supervision sit OUTSIDE the core.
executionCore.falsifiedBy: a core that can grant a capability, resolve a contribution, or spawn a process

knownLimitations: 130 of 135 findings are STILL-OPEN. That is the honest state.

The v2 denominator was produced by regex over prose and was wrong — the same lexical-enumeration error as Error 1 and the authorship misattribution. Eighth instance of inferring a set from a pattern instead of reading the source.
Authored solo by the agent whose work the correction indicts.
Five of nineteen invariants were defective on first substantive review. The set survived several packaging rounds without anyone testing whether it was RIGHT.
EC-3 required a second correction in v5: v4 conflated content-derived RunId with per-attempt ExecutionId. Extraction and later adjudication did not carry the R-1 identity distinction forward.

reviewerDisagreements.note: Three head-to-head disagreements. A1 marked TO-7, TO-11 and EC-3 correct; B found each defective. Adjudicated individually, not by majority or deference.
reviewerDisagreements.outcome: B upheld on all three — but in two, A1's reading was also correct about a different half and is preserved (TO-7b, and the retained clause of TO-11).
reviewerDisagreements.lesson: An invariant true only under a charitable reading is defective. A1 read charitably and found no fault; B read literally and found three. Literal reading is the correct standard for an invariant.
